newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla plunges to burden Oslo Total index.
newsitem.headline: Orkla plunges to burden Oslo Total index.

text.p: Shares in food-based conglomerate Orkla, Norway's second largest listed company, slipped on Tuesday to help drag down the Total index at the Norwegian stock exchange.
The index, which soared to a record close on Monday, finished 0.46 percent lower at 1,182.55 points after reaching an intra-day high of 1,189.37 points in the morning.
"The entire fall of the Total index can be blamed on Orkla's decline," a market player said. "It makes the rest of the market become very cautious and volume is low."

Orkla has plunged around 10 percent since announcing disappointing four-month results last Thursday. The company's A share closed 4.2 percent, or 25 crowns, off at 548 crowns in turnover worth 54.7 million crowns.
Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner's A share was the most traded stock at 161 million crowns. It closed 0.59 percent off at 424 crowns.
Industrial group Norsk Hydro, Norway's largest listed company, was the second most traded share at 104 million crowns. The share rose 0.39 percent to 385 crowns.
